verdict.headline: S&P 500 closes at its first record since August as the ten-year eases, but long bonds hold
verdict.label: Close Tue: S&P 500 7,818.93 (+0.58%, record), Nasdaq 27,599.79 (+0.45%, record), Dow +0.49%, Russell 2000 -0.59%; VIX 15.01; 10Y ~5.27% (-5 bp), 30Y ~5.66% (flat, above 5.644%); Brent $100.58, WTI $89.44; 3Y auction 4.932%, 2.62 bid-to-cover.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: the S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,818.93, its first close above 7,800 and first record since August 13, and the Nasdaq set a second straight record. The ten-year Treasury yield fell about 5 basis points to 5.27% and the $58 billion three-year auction cleared near average at 4.932%, though indirect bidders took only 57.6% against a 65.9% average. The thirty-year held near 5.66%, above the 5.644% 2002 high it broke on Monday. The Russell 2000 fell 0.59%. Oil's pre-market decline reversed: Brent settled up 26 cents at $100.58.

What it means: the record rests on lower intermediate yields and AI spending news (Google's 20-year Constellation nuclear deal, Marvell's raised outlook, Nvidia near $6 trillion), not on broad relief. The long end did not join in, and the ten-to-thirty-year spread widened to about 39 basis points, which points to a supply or inflation premium the record has not yet had to absorb.

What would change the picture: a weak thirty-year auction on Thursday would support the supply explanation; a thirty-year close under 5.644% would undo Monday's break, a close above 5.703% would extend it. A ten-year close above 5.349% with the index at a record would show stocks carrying higher yields; an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show it following them. Note: news sites could not be opened from this run, so figures rest on search summaries of the cited sources.
verdict.lede_short: The S&P 500 closed at its first record since August as the ten-year Treasury yield eased to 5.27%, led by chipmakers and Google's nuclear power deal with Constellation. The relief was partial: the thirty-year stayed above its 2002 high and small caps fell, so the record rests on a few large AI names. Thursday's thirty-year auction is the test; a close above 5.703% would put the long-bond pressure back on the record.

supporting_data.label: The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to a record 7,818.93, its first close above 7,800 and first record since August 13 — while the Russell 2000 fell 0.59%, so the gain came from a narrow group of large stocks.

The ten-year yield eased about 5 basis points to 5.27% while the thirty-year held near 5.66% — the long end stayed above its 2002 high and the ten-to-thirty-year spread widened to about 39 basis points.

The $58 billion three-year sale cleared at 4.932% with a 2.62 bid-to-cover against a 2.65 average and indirects at 57.6% against 65.9% — the sale passed, but the buyers usually read as foreign demand were thinner before the ten- and thirty-year auctions.

Google agreed a 20-year deal to buy 3,590 megawatts from 11 Constellation nuclear units, funding $4.3 billion of upgrades with first power in 2028 — Constellation rose as much as 15% and lifted the nuclear group.
Brent settled up 26 cents at $100.58 and WTI up 1 cent at $89.44 after Brent traded under $99 before the open — attacks on tankers near Hormuz kept the morning's decline from lasting.
Marvell rose about 6% after raising its fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenue outlook at its investor day, and Broadcom about 4% — the market read the custom AI chip case as good news for the whole category.

watchlist_mentions.note: Rose again toward a $6 trillion market value, which needs a share price near $250, about 5% above Monday's record $238.90 close.
Rose nearly 3% to a record alongside Nvidia as chipmakers led the S&P 500 to its first record since August.
Agreed a 20-year deal for 3,590 megawatts from 11 Constellation nuclear units, with first power in 2028 — a long-dated commitment to AI power supply.
Rose about 4% to $376.09 as Marvell's investor day made the case for custom AI chips.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year held near 5.66%, above its 5.644% 2002 high, while the ten-year eased 5 basis points; the three-year auction drew thinner indirect demand (57.6% against a 65.9% average). Thursday's $22 billion thirty-year sale tests whether the long end carries a supply premium.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year ~5.66% between Monday's 5.703% intraday high and the 5.644% 2002 high.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 5.644% would undo Monday's break; a close above 5.703%, especially after a weak auction, would extend it.
trade_setups.horizon: October 7-9, through the ten- and thirty-year auctions

trade_setups.thesis: Seagate and Western Digital fell about 8% and 6% by late morning, after roughly 10% drops on Friday, on Toshiba's plan to double hard-drive capacity by fiscal 2027 — the first direct supply threat to the scarcity behind their 2026 gains.
trade_setups.entry: Seagate near $819 and Western Digital near $415 in late-morning trading.
trade_setups.invalidation: Stabilisation with Micron flat would mark the move as specific to drives rather than storage demand; further losses in Micron would widen it to memory.
